Tolkien and compiled by the efforts of many, most notably Christopher Tolkien and the authors of Parma Eldalamberon and Vinyar Tengwar (Christopher Gilson, Carl Hostetter, Arden Smith, Bill Welden, Patrick Wynne, and others).

Paul Strack's Eldamo lexicon attempts to consistently organize that material, which adds up to many thousands of words in nearly fifty languages. This app is meant as a handy tool to search and access this vocabulary. 

Features: 
- very comprehensive: contains the complete Eldamo.org vocabulary (48 languages)
- searching for either Elvish words or English translations
- several search modes: wildcard (diacritic-insensitive), strict (diacritic-sensitive), begin- and end-of-word matching (useful to find rhyming words), verbatim and regular expressions
- includes community-created words (neo-Sindarin, neo-Quenya)
- roots, archaic words, community-contributed words and word reliability (is a word attested or speculative) are indicated by color coding
- tapping a word opens a detail screen with glosses, examples, inflections, changes, cognates, elements, related words, variations and notes (when available)
- where applicable: tapping a linked word in a detail category or the notes opens the detail screen for that word
- configuration settings are stored locally in the app until changed
- no internet connection is required

- other translations besides English (most likely German and French first)

- extras like an Elvish / Shire calendar, star- and constellation names
